overview: This lesson introduces students to the human digestive system, focusing on the major organs involved in the process. Students will learn to identify these organs and trace the continuous path that food takes through the alimentary canal from ingestion to excretion.
objectives: [Remember] Identify the major organs of the human digestive system including the oral cavity, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine.
[Understand] Trace the sequential path of food through the alimentary canal from the mouth to the anus.
[Apply] Relate the anatomical positions of digestive organs to their proper sequence in the journey of food.

activities.title: What Happens to Our Food?
activities.description: Initiate a class discussion about what students think happens to food after they eat it. Ask them to name any body parts involved. This activates prior knowledge and sets the stage for the lesson.

activities.title: Digestive Organ Arrangement Challenge
activities.description: Provide students with cut-outs of the major digestive organs (oral cavity, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, liver, pancreas, gallbladder) and ask them to arrange them in the sequence they think food travels, or in their correct anatomical positions, on a large sheet of paper. Encourage group discussion.
materials: Printed cut-outs of digestive organs (mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, liver, gallbladder, pancreas)
Large chart paper or individual worksheets

activities.title: Journey Through the System: Teacher-led Explanation
activities.description: Using a projected or large physical diagram of the human digestive system, the teacher will systematically point out and name each major organ (oral cavity, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum/anus) and accessory organs (liver, gallbladder, pancreas) while tracing the path of food. Emphasize the continuous nature of the alimentary canal and the relative positions of organs as seen in the diagram.
materials: Projector or large print diagram of the human digestive system (similar to source content)

activities.title: Food's Journey Map
activities.description: Students will individually draw a simplified diagram of the human digestive system, labeling at least five major organs. Alternatively, they can create a flow chart or list detailing the sequence of organs food passes through, starting from the oral cavity and ending at the anus.

activities.title: Quick Check-in: Exit Ticket
activities.description: Students answer a few questions on an 'exit ticket' to assess their understanding of organ identification and the path of food.

assessment:
1. [Remember] List five major organs of the human digestive system.
2. [Understand] Describe the complete path taken by a morsel of food, naming at least six distinct organs, from the moment it enters the oral cavity until waste is eliminated.
3. [Apply] Imagine you are a tiny food particle. Explain your journey through the oral cavity, pharynx, and esophagus, describing the order in which you would pass through them.
